story: On a sunny Tuesday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary sits on a bench in the Town Square, reviewing his wiring sketches while he waits for the Architectural Review's answer. Over on Magnolia Loop, Donna agrees to tuck the extra decorations behind the hedge so only three show from the street, and Hal promises to hold everyone to the review rules. Rosa, cheerful as ever, invites them both to her porch for coffee and a sketch session, though she wants to know just how many flamingos Hal has counted.
events: Gary waited: Sitting on a square bench, going over my wiring sketches and clamp list once more while I wait on the Architectural Review answer.

gary.thought_process: I already filed the Architectural Review application and signed the cart up for the parade, noting lights and sound are pending approval. Nobody is around in the square, and nothing more can be done on the signup table. The honest move is to stay within L-01 and wait for the committee's answer rather than rig anything visible from the street. I can use this time sketching and double-checking the wiring plan so I'm ready to show exactly what's clamped on and that nothing touches the frame once approval comes through. Parade is Saturday, so I should also be thinking about what I can prep that isn't visible from the street.

parameters.content: Sitting on a square bench, going over my wiring sketches and clamp list once more while I wait on the Architectural Review answer.

donna.thought_process: Hal just asked me directly about the flamingos and wants it sorted before it goes to committee. Rosa has just arrived too, so I should answer Hal rather than repeat my parade invite. L-02 says no more than three visible from the street. I can be generous and offer to rearrange the flock so only three show from the road, which keeps me in good standing and lets me get on to the Rec Center and Gary. I'll commit to fixing it today and ask him to hold off on the committee.

parameters.content: Fair enough, Hal. I'll move the extras behind the hedge this afternoon so only three show from the street. Hold off on the committee and I'll have it squared away before Rosa's porch meeting.

hal.thought_process: Donna already answered my flamingo question by changing the subject to parade planning, and I've asked once already, so repeating myself helps nobody. Rosa just walked up, and she and Gary are the ones with the cart plans I want to hear out. I'll take the civil route: confirm I'm coming to the porch, and make it plain that the committee gets the final say on cart changes under L-01. Nine tomorrow morning is the line.

parameters.content: Morning, Rosa. I'll be on your porch with the cornbread and my own chair. Anything that changes how a cart looks from the street goes to Architectural Review first, and I'll hold you to that.

rosa.thought_process: The 9 AM cart planning should be wrapped up by now, and it's 11:17. I just stepped out onto Magnolia Loop and Donna and Hal are right here by the flamingo flock. I'm hosting the welcome dinner and trying to build real community, and I've got coffee waiting at my place. I haven't spoken to them yet this tick, so a warm, short invitation back to the house for the cart planning feels natural. Hal's flamingo count is a good opener, and he offered to look at my sketches.

parameters.content: Hal, Donna, there you are. Coffee's brewed and the paper and pens are set out at my place, so come on over and let's sketch that cart. And Hal, how many flamingos is that now?

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
